description: GET /sessions/{id}/page: the active tab as numbered elements and text. Secret fields (password, one-time code, card) carry value_hidden and never their value. challenges lists only check frames the person can see: a non-empty box in the viewport, not hidden. An element may carry context (the names of up to two containers around it, innermost last, joined by ' › ') and in_dialog (true inside an open dialog). elements never lists a frame. Past the cap it lists the on-screen elements ahead of the off-screen ones, each group in page order, and truncated says more elements exist than are listed; when every shown element fits, a host may keep page order or use the same order. A host may list an open dialog's elements (in_dialog) ahead of both groups. text is the page's text cut at max_text when the page isn't scrolled or the text fits; otherwise it starts at the top of the view after a leading '…', and the start of the text above the view follows when the budget allows. A secret editor's text is never in text or in any name, and max_text 0 gives ''. frames lists the page's rendered child frames, on-screen first: url (origin and path for http and https, about:blank or about:srcdoc, otherwise the scheme alone), read, box (the frame's content box in screenshot pixels, null when the host can't place it), offscreen (true when it is out of view), and for a read frame its elements, text and truncated. Frame elements are read-only: no id and no field value (a select keeps its value and options), so a step reaches them only by position, and a type with focused true reaches the field the focus is in. A frame is never read when it is a human check, a consent page, on a payment_frame_hosts or sign_in_frame_hosts host or under one, holds a secret, card-named or sign-in field, or is under frame_min_read_px either way, and a host leaves unread a frame it finds the person can't see. A host reads at most frames_read frames, in the order frames lists them, and a frame it leaves unread for any of these reasons takes none of them. A read frame lists at most elements_per_frame elements and text_per_frame characters of text. A host that places and reads frames apart from the page's own read gives them at most frames_phase_ms from the read's start; a frame that doesn't answer in time is listed unread, with box null.
